title: Moving a group, not its points
question: If the Drawing library's picture were a tree of groups, each with a transform, instead of a flat list of polygons, how much smaller would a slider's picture diff be, and would the computation follow? Built for one slide, Full Body, as ^report(11)'s What next, step 1 asked.

builds.name: measuring build
builds.note: with ^report(11)'s oracle on a local branch, not pushed, and two more of its modes: one exports each edit's picture, and one measures another expression in the picture's place (here, the tree instead of its flattening)

slide: full-body-groups.hz, an experimental copy of the Livelit Playground's Full Body slide (not in the Hazel repository; it is in this report's folder, 012/full-body-groups.hz): a Scene type of leaves and groups, each group with an affine transform (a b c d e f, as SVG's matrix), a flatten that composes them, and the figure's parts placed, armed, handed and eyed as groups. Its picture is flatten(scene).

versions.today's picture: full-body.hz as it is: a flat list of 49 polygons, every point in absolute coordinates
versions.groups, flattened: full-body-groups.hz's picture, flatten(scene), as the slide shows it
versions.groups, not flattened: the tree itself (scene) measured in the picture's place: 82 nodes, 49 shapes and 33 groups; what a renderer that draws groups would take

runtime: node, the test build. Versions not stated in the report.
edits: the 27 slider edits of ^report(11) on Full Body, each moved by a fifth of its range; each edit's slider, label, old and new value are in its ladder line
runs: The slide cut at its picture, analyzed with Statics.mk_unmemoized, evaluated from scratch and incrementally, as in ^report(11), for each of the three versions. Today's picture was measured again on the same build as the tree; it matches ^report(11)'s run step for step (its ladder lines are identical to the Full Body lines of 011/data/ladder011.output). Steps are deterministic, so one run of each suffices; every control is clean.

measures.picture diff, today (shapes): count: the shapes of the flat picture (49) the edit changes; for an edit that changes how many shapes there are, no shape-by-shape count ('changes the count')
measures.picture diff, groups (nodes): count: the nodes of the tree (82: 49 shapes and 33 groups) the edit changes. A group counts as changed when its transform does, a shape when its points or style do; a group's children are matched by their longest common subsequence, and a node on one side only counts with everything in it. Differences below 10^-9 count as none, in both pictures.
measures.trace distance (steps): count: the fewest evaluation steps any update could take again, estimated from above by keying calls on their content, as in ^report(11): the incremental run's steps less the steps of its outermost calls matched by content. On today's picture, the tree flattened at the end, and the tree not flattened.
measures.Hazel's update (steps): count: the steps of Hazel's incremental run after the edit, on today's picture and on the tree not flattened (the table's columns); the flattened tree's is in the text for an arm-angle edit (128,194) and in its ladder file for every edit
measures.from scratch (steps): count: the steps to draw the figure from scratch: today's picture 121,973, the tree flattened 148,217, the tree alone 110,260
measures.Hazel's update, as a share: % of the version's own run from scratch, in the text only: 85.2 to 89.0% on today's picture and 81.5 to 87.7% on the tree not flattened, for the edits of Figure 2
measures.flattened against today: the largest coordinate difference, point by point, between the tree flattened and today's picture, over 28 pictures (before each edit and after): within 6x10^-14

times: not timed: steps, counted as the evaluator takes them; in steps, not shares, since the three versions take different numbers of steps from scratch

raw_files.data/ladder012_today.output: Today's picture (full-body.hz) on the same build as the tree: a CONTROL line and the 27 edits as tab-separated LADDER lines, in ^report(11)'s format (011/data/meta.json describes it): 'LADDER <slide>', slider, label, old value, new value, 'shapes <before> <after> same <n>', then 'SCRATCH' and 'TODAY', each 'executed E in_calls C calls N content K' and, per naming scheme, '<scheme> skip S reads R cells L | equal a notEqual b onlyLeft c onlyRight d collisions e'. The trace distance is the TODAY run's E less its K; Hazel's update is the TODAY run's E.
raw_files.data/ladder012_groups_flattened.output: The same for full-body-groups.hz, its picture flatten(scene): the tree flattened at the end.
raw_files.data/ladder012_groups_not_flattened.outp: The same for full-body-groups.hz with the tree itself (scene) measured in the picture's place. Its 'shapes 17 17 same 0' field compares the scene's 17 top-level items and reads 0 on every edit, even one that changes nothing; the report does not use it (the tree's picture diff is in picture_diff012.json).
raw_files.data/picture_diff012.json: The picture diff of each edit: a JSON list of {name, flat, flat_shapes, tree, tree_nodes}: the shapes the edit changes in the flat picture (null when it changes how many there are) out of flat_shapes (49), and the nodes it changes in the tree out of tree_nodes (82), compared as described under the measures. Made by a script from the exported pictures of every edit, flat and tree (2 x 28 JSON files, about 2.5 MB, not kept here). Figure 2 and the table's first two columns.
raw_files.data/tree012_before.json: The tree before any edit, as exported: a JSON list of the scene's 17 top-level items, {same, shape}, each shape a Group, {name, transform: {a, b, c, d, e, f}, children}, or a Leaf holding a Drawing shape ({ctor: Polygon | Path, arg: {name, points: [{at: [x, y], label}], stroke, fill}}), in the group's own coordinates. Figures 1, 3 and 4 are drawn from it.
raw_files.data/tree012_drivers.json: For each node of the tree, keyed by its path of child indices from the top-level item ('13,0,1,0'), the sliders whose edit changes it (a group's name or transform, a leaf's name, points, fill or stroke); '(new)' after a slider marks a node that exists only after its edit. Made from the exported pictures; Figures 1 and 3 say what places and shapes each part from it.

provenance.flattened against today: Exists only as printed: the check that the flattened tree draws today's picture to within 6x10^-14 in all 28 pictures. The script that compared them printed its result; the exported pictures it compared are not kept here.
provenance.the slide: 012/full-body-groups.hz, next to this folder, is the experimental slide the tree versions were measured on.
